explanation_bullets: Exit Load is a statutory charge levied by the Asset Management Company (AMC) if mutual fund units are redeemed before a mandated holding period.
For Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs), each monthly installment carries its own individual holding clock measured from its unique allotment date.
Redemptions strictly adhere to First-In, First-Out (FIFO) accounting, liquidating oldest purchased units first.
Exit load is credited directly back to the fund scheme to safeguard continuing long-term investors, not retained as platform brokerage.
Applicable Goods and Services Tax (GST) of 18% is levied on the exit load amount as required by statutory tax regulations.
Certain categories (e.g., overnight funds, liquid funds held past 7 days, or equity funds held past 365 days) carry nil exit load once their holding period is completed.

Exit load is a charge levied by the mutual fund when units are redeemed before a specified holding period, as defined in the scheme’s offer document.
The load is applied only at the time of redemption, not for intra‑day transactions; mutual funds do not allow intra‑day exits, so no load is charged for same‑day trades.
The percentage shown in the app reflects the load applicable for the remaining holding period and cannot exceed the maximum rate disclosed in the scheme’s prospectus.
Exit load is a regulatory charge mandated by SEBI, not a hidden fee; the amount and conditions are published in the scheme information document.

Brokerage is the fee charged by the broker for executing each purchase or sale of mutual fund units and is calculated per transaction segment, not as a single flat charge on the total investment.
The fee is disclosed in the transaction statement; GST of 18% is applied on the brokerage amount and shown separately, so there are no hidden taxes beyond the GST.
Brokerage rates are determined by the broker and may be revised periodically; any change is communicated through official notices and is not applied without prior disclosure.
Brokerage is distinct from exit load: brokerage is levied at the time of trade, whereas exit load is a redemption charge applied after a specified holding period.
For SIPs, each installment has its own holding period; if an installment is redeemed before its period ends, the applicable exit load is charged only on that installment.
GST at 18% is also levied on the exit load amount, and this tax is reflected in the redemption statement.
Exit load is a charge levied by a mutual fund when units are redeemed before a specified holding period; it does not apply to equity trades or brokerage fees.
The percentage of exit load varies by scheme and is disclosed in the scheme’s offer document; it is not a fixed rate across all funds.
A load is only waived if the redemption occurs after the fund‑specified minimum holding period; the waiver is scheme‑specific and not automatically applied by the platform.

Exit load is distinct from brokerage or transaction fees, which are charged by brokers for buying or selling securities and are unrelated to mutual fund redemption charges.

The load is not a hidden fee; it is disclosed in the scheme information memorandum and on transaction statements at the time of purchase and redemption.

Brokerage is a fee charged by the broker for executing each trade; it varies per transaction and is not a single flat amount for all trades.
The fee amount is disclosed before order confirmation and appears on the trade confirmation statement; it is not hidden.

Brokerage rates are set by the broker and may differ for equity, derivatives, and mutual fund transactions; mutual fund purchases typically incur a transaction charge rather than traditional brokerage.
Higher brokerage fees are generally linked to the volume or value of the trade, not to a separate platform subscription fee.
